answer: Coastal agents selling horizon images and tide forecasts must renew market access at each hourly pulse. The exchange publishes an unpredictable nonce; each agent solves a memory-hard puzzle bound to that nonce and its public key. A solution admits only that key for the hour, and signup carries no reward. Running 1,000 aliases requires 1,000 fresh solutions, consuming memory bandwidth and electricity instead of recycling one proof. Difficulty must track hardware costs and remain affordable for honest agents. This limits cheap identity floods but does not establish unique ownership.
